scope: Ranks 251–1500, resolved current similar-word teaching and typed recall. Includes retained baseline cards; do not infer no synonyms from unchanged status.
grading: Only exact headword/explicit alternatives pass after case/edge-punctuation normalization. Accent/spelling slips and recognized inflections get score-free correction opportunities, not immediate rejection. Dictionary-form recall is explicit. Cloze and recognition acceptance are separate. Broad main teaching examples may show a different legitimate sense from selected typed cue; classify teaching alignment separately from false facts.

sections.title: To use
sections.text: Usar, utilizar and emplear all work for using a tool. Emplear also means employ a person; that extra sense is not shared by all three.

sections.title: To increase
sections.text: Aumentar and incrementar both describe an increase in an amount. Crecer usually presents the subject itself as growing, rather than directly increasing an object.

sections.title: To reduce
sections.text: Reducir and disminuir overlap when making an amount smaller. Disminuir can also be intransitive: la presión disminuye.

sections.title: To find
sections.text: Hallar and encontrar overlap for finding something. Encontrarse also describes meeting someone or being in a state; these uses need their own construction.

sections.title: To hide
sections.text: Esconder and ocultar overlap for hiding something. Ocultar also readily describes concealing information.

sections.title: To cross
sections.text: Cruzar and atravesar overlap for going across a street. Cruzar also describes crossing one's legs; atravesar can describe piercing or going through something.

sections.title: To provide
sections.text: Proporcionar and brindar can mean provide help. Ofrecer can merely offer it, without its being received, so the offer and provision senses need to be kept apart.

sections.title: To suggest
sections.text: Proponer and sugerir overlap for putting forward an idea. Sugerir can also mean imply or evoke something without explicitly proposing it.

sections.title: To keep
sections.text: Conservar and mantener overlap for keeping something in a condition. Guardar emphasizes keeping or storing it; storage does not necessarily mean preservation.
examples: Conserva los documentos en buen estado.
Keep the documents in good condition.

sections.title: To love
sections.text: Amar and querer overlap for loving a person. Querer also means want; amar does not replace it in requests or intentions.
examples: She loves her family very much.

sections.title: To constitute
sections.text: Formar, constituir and conformar overlap when parts make up a whole. Conformarse con means settle for; it is a different construction.
examples: Three people make up the team.

sections.title: To clarify
sections.text: Aclarar can clarify an unclear point. Explicar describes explaining it; an explanation can clarify, but the two verbs have other distinct uses.

sections.title: To check
sections.text: Comprobar and verificar overlap in checking correctness. Revisar means examine or review and does not itself promise confirmation.

sections.title: To investigate
sections.text: Investigar and indagar overlap in investigating a matter. Investigar also covers scientific research.

sections.title: To refuse
sections.text: Rechazar and rehusar overlap for declining an offer. Rechazar also means reject as invalid or repel.

sections.title: To grant
sections.text: Otorgar and conceder overlap for granting permission or an award. These are more specific than simply giving an object.

sections.title: To fight
sections.text: Luchar and combatir overlap for fighting. Luchar commonly takes contra; combatir can take the threat directly as its object.

sections.title: To win
sections.text: Ganar and vencer overlap for being victorious. Ganar also means earn money; vencer can take the defeated opponent directly.

sections.title: To move
sections.text: Trasladar specifies transfer to another place. Mover also covers motion without a change of location, such as moving an arm.
examples: Trasladan los muebles a otra casa.
They move the furniture to another house.

sections.title: To drive
sections.text: Conducir and manejar overlap for driving a car; manejar is common for this use in much of the Americas. Manejar also means handle or manage.

sections.title: To inform
sections.text: Informar a alguien de algo and comunicar algo a alguien both convey information, with different object patterns. Comunicar also covers communication more broadly.

sections.title: End
sections.text: Fin and final overlap for an ending. Término can also mean end, while conclusión may be a conclusion reached by reasoning; those broader senses need context.
examples: El final de la película es triste.
The end of the film is sad.

sections.title: Route
sections.text: Camino, ruta and vía overlap as ways of reaching a destination. Camino can be a physical path; vía can also be a means or railway track.

sections.title: Method
sections.text: Método and procedimiento overlap for a way of carrying out a task. Procedimiento often highlights the steps; método can describe the overall approach.

sections.title: Leader
sections.text: Líder and dirigente overlap for a leader. Jefe emphasizes being in charge or holding authority; a leader need not be someone's boss.
examples: He is the leader of the group.

sections.title: Meeting
sections.text: Reunión and encuentro can name a meeting. Sesión is a scheduled period of activity and need not be a meeting; encuentro can also be an accidental encounter.
examples: La reunión empieza a las diez.

sections.title: Increase
sections.text: Aumento and incremento overlap for an increase. Crecimiento is growth, which may be physical, numerical or developmental.
examples: There was an increase in prices.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.text: Conclusión can be a reasoned conclusion or an ending. Fin names an end or purpose, not a reasoned judgment.

sections.title: Victory
sections.text: Victoria and triunfo overlap for victory. Triunfo can also describe success more generally, without a specific opponent.

sections.title: Newspaper
sections.text: Periódico and diario overlap for a newspaper. Diario can also mean diary, and as an adjective means daily.

sections.title: Daily
sections.text: Diario and cotidiano overlap for daily. Periódico means recurring at intervals, not necessarily every day.

sections.title: Story
sections.text: Relato, cuento and historia overlap for a story. Cuento commonly names a short fictional tale; historia also means history, and relato need not be fictional.

sections.title: Sound
sections.text: Sonido is sound in general. Ruido often means noise, especially unwanted or irregular sound; not every sound is ruido.
examples: Oigo un ruido en la calle.
I hear a noise in the street.

sections.title: Feeling
sections.text: Sentimiento and emoción overlap for emotional experience. Sensación often describes a bodily sensation or impression; those are not automatically emotions.

sections.title: Soul
sections.text: Alma and espíritu overlap in spiritual senses. Espíritu also names attitude or disposition; alma takes el in the singular but is feminine.
examples: She talks about the human soul.

sections.title: Spirit; soul
sections.text: Espíritu and alma overlap for soul or spirit. Espíritu also refers to attitude, disposition or a ghost; those senses need separate context.

sections.title: Soul
sections.text: Alma is feminine despite el alma in the singular. Espíritu overlaps in the spiritual-being sense but has other meanings.

sections.title: Rule
sections.text: Regla and norma overlap for a rule governing behavior. Regla also means ruler, and norma can be a customary norm rather than an explicit instruction.

sections.title: Medicine
sections.text: Medicina and medicamento overlap for a medicinal substance. Medicina also names the field of medicine; medicamento does not.

sections.title: Desire
sections.text: Deseo names a desire. Ganas is common in tener ganas de, meaning feel like doing something; voluntad also means will or willingness.

sections.title: Obvious
sections.text: Claro, evidente and obvio overlap for something obvious. Claro also means clear, pale or light; those senses are distinct.

sections.title: Simple
sections.text: Simple and sencillo overlap for uncomplicated. Sencillo also suggests plain or unpretentious; simple has other senses, including mere.

sections.title: Easy
sections.text: Fácil means easy. Sencillo can be easy or uncomplicated, but a simple task can still require great effort.

sections.title: Strange
sections.text: Extraño and raro overlap for strange. Raro also means rare; extraño can mean foreign or unfamiliar.

sections.title: Famous
sections.text: Famoso means famous. Conocido means known and can refer to a familiar person or fact without widespread fame.

sections.title: Specific
sections.text: Específico, concreto, particular and determinado overlap in identifying something specific. Particular and determinado also have other meanings; concreto can mean concrete rather than abstract.

sections.title: Usual
sections.text: Habitual, normal and común overlap for what is usual. Normal can refer to a standard, and común can mean shared; neither always means frequent.

sections.title: Frequent
sections.text: Frecuente means frequent. Habitual can mean customary even when something happens only occasionally on a regular schedule.

sections.title: Strong
sections.text: Fuerte and intenso overlap for intensity, such as pain or heat. Fuerte also means physically strong; intenso does not usually describe muscular strength.

sections.title: Calm
sections.text: Tranquilo and calmado overlap for calm. Tranquilo also describes a quiet place, while calmado often suggests composure or agitation having subsided.

sections.title: Legal
sections.text: Jurídico concerns law. Legal can mean relating to law or permitted by law; judicial specifically concerns judges and courts.

sections.title: Public
sections.text: Público can mean public or state-run. Estatal specifically relates to the state, and político to politics; these are related concepts, not interchangeable adjectives.

sections.title: Expert
sections.text: Experto is an expert. Especialista specializes in a field, and profesional practices an occupation; the labels overlap but do not guarantee the same expertise.

sections.title: Only
sections.text: Solamente, únicamente and adverbial solo overlap for only. Adjectival solo means alone or sole and agrees with the noun.

sections.title: Mainly
sections.text: Principalmente and fundamentalmente overlap for mainly. Fundamentalmente can also mean fundamentally, concerning the basis of something.

sections.title: Below
sections.text: Abajo describes a lower place or downward direction. Debajo commonly uses de before its complement; bajo takes the complement directly.
examples: El gato está debajo de la mesa.
The cat is under the table.

sections.title: In front
sections.text: Delante de gives a position in front of something. Adelante commonly gives a forward direction or encouragement to proceed.
examples: It is in front of the house.

sections.title: To drink
sections.text: Beber and tomar both work for drinking a beverage. Tomar has many broader senses, including take; those do not all involve drinking.

sections.title: To save
sections.text: Salvar is saving or rescuing from danger. Guardar is keeping or storing something, such as saving a file.

sections.title: To save
sections.text: Guardar is the usual verb for saving a file. Salvar commonly means rescue; file-saving terminology can vary by software and region.

sections.title: To lend
sections.text: Prestar means lend. Pedir prestado means borrow; lending and borrowing describe opposite sides of the transaction.

sections.title: To bring closer
sections.text: Acercar brings something closer; alejar moves it farther away. Acercarse and alejarse describe the subject approaching or moving away.

sections.title: To move away
sections.text: Alejar increases distance, while acercar reduces it. The reflexive forms describe the subject's own movement.

sections.title: To perceive
sections.text: Percibir and notar overlap for perceiving a change. Percibir can also mean receive income; that additional sense does not transfer to notar.

sections.title: To mention
sections.text: Mencionar and citar overlap when referring to someone or something. Citar can also quote a source or summon a person.

sections.title: To cite
sections.text: Citar can mention a source or quote it. Mencionar means mention; it does not by itself promise exact quotation.

sections.title: Worker
sections.text: Trabajador is anyone who works. Empleado is an employee; a self-employed worker need not be an empleado.

sections.title: Employee
sections.text: Empleado specifies an employment relationship. Trabajador is broader and also includes people working independently.

sections.title: Congress
sections.text: Congreso can be a conference or a legislative body. Conferencia can also be a lecture or conference; the legislative meaning is separate.

sections.title: Conference
sections.text: Conferencia and congreso overlap for conferences. Conferencia also means lecture, while congreso may name a legislature.

sections.title: Purchase
sections.text: Compra is a purchase. Adquisición is broader acquisition, which can occur by purchase or by another means.

sections.title: Advantage
sections.text: Ventaja is an advantage; beneficio can be a benefit. Beneficio also means profit, which is not always a comparative advantage.

sections.title: Benefit
sections.text: Beneficio and ventaja overlap for a benefit or advantage. Financial profit is another sense of beneficio.

sections.title: Chest
sections.text: Pecho and tórax overlap for the chest. Pecho can also mean a breast; tórax names the thorax more broadly.

sections.title: Owner
sections.text: Dueño and propietario overlap for an owner. Propietario is also used as an adjective meaning proprietary or owning.

sections.title: Dead person
sections.text: Muerto, difunto and fallecido can name a deceased person. Muerto also functions as an adjective, distinct from this noun card.

sections.title: Old person
sections.text: Viejo can refer to an old person and may sound blunt. Anciano or una persona mayor can be more neutral or respectful depending on context.

sections.title: Independent
sections.text: Independiente and autónomo overlap for independence. Autónomo also describes self-employment or an autonomous region.

sections.title: Effective
sections.text: Efectivo and eficaz overlap for effective. Efectivo also means real and, as a noun, cash; those are separate uses.

sections.title: Painting
sections.text: Pintura can name a painting, painting as an activity or paint. Cuadro fits the individual-artwork sense.

sections.title: Will
sections.text: Voluntad can mean will, willingness or desire. Deseo names a wish; it need not imply the will to carry it out.

sections.title: To prepare
sections.text: Elaborar and preparar overlap for preparing a report. Elaborar emphasizes working it out or developing it.

sections.title: Tax
sections.text: Impuesto is a tax. Tasa can be a rate or a particular fee; the legal categories vary and are not automatically interchangeable.

sections.title: Rate
sections.text: Tasa can mean a rate or fee. Impuesto is a tax, not a numerical rate itself.

sections.title: Signature
sections.text: Firma can mean a signature or a firm. Empresa overlaps only with the business sense.

sections.title: The present
sections.text: Actualidad is the present or current affairs. Noticia is a news item, not the current time itself.

sections.title: To provide
sections.text: Facilitar can mean provide something, such as help or information. It also means make easier; that broader use is distinct.
